newsitem.title: USA: Clinton sets community service summit on April 27.
newsitem.headline: Clinton sets community service summit on April 27.

text.p: With former President George Bush at his side, President Clinton announced Friday plans for a "presidents summit" meeting on community service in Philadelphia on April 27.

"Much of the work of America cannot be done by government; much of the work cannot be done by government alone," Clinton said in a White House ceremony. "The solution must be the American people through voluntary service to others."

Clinton said Colin Powell, former chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, would be the general chairman of the summit, which is designed to inspire Americans to devote more time to volunteer community service.

"The things which unite us as citizens are bigger than any one person, one party, one election or one ideology," Clinton said, striking the themes of cooperation and bipartisanship he has sounded since his re-election. "They can only be solved if we come together in partnership to lift each other up."
Bush, whom Clinton defeated for the presidency in 1992, echoed the president's remarks.

"When it comes to addressing many of the problems we face as a nation, it isn't a question of partisan poltics, of one side against another, it's a question of all pulling together for the common good," Bush said.
